included.reason: I-SPEED (screening code confirmed at full text; the only quantitative comparison with a classical method is the iteration-count acceleration ratio against the standard two-level SIMP with a uniform initial guess, Table 5)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Warm-starting cell-level SIMP with the nearest archived optimised cell (energy-based similarity, augmented 15,744-sample dataset) instead of a uniform density cuts the mean SIMP iteration count on the held-out 2D Hook problem by a factor of 2.67 (Table 5).
claim.key_phrase: placing it closer to a local minimum and reducing computation time
claim.location: Section 4 (Results), Table 5 (p. 17), with the per-cell results of Figs. 16-17, 20-21, 24, 27-28; the abstract and conclusions (Sec. 6, pp. 21-23) state the acceleration only qualitatively. Chosen under §5.1 rules 2 and 4: Table 5 is the article's summary of the acceleration, and the energy-based metric with Dataset Index 3 and augmentation is the configuration the conclusions recommend
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Stated as the average acceleration ratio beta (Eqs. 6-7, p. 13; Table 5, p. 17), where beta = n_standard/n_model for accelerated cells and -n_model/n_standard for decelerated ones; 2.67 is the energy-based metric with Dataset Index 3 plus augmentation. Table 5 ranges from 1.34 (Index 1, L2, no augmentation) to 2.86 (Index 3, L2, augmentation); L1 gives 2.80 in the same row. It is an iteration-count ratio, not a time: no run time appears anywhere. Averaging the piecewise beta over cells is not the ratio of total iterations, so the total-cost saving may differ [inferred]. Dataset construction is excluded.
claim.alternatives: (1) Table 5, L2-based norm, Dataset Index 3 with augmentation: 2.86, the highest tabulated value. (2) Table 5 without augmentation: 1.34-1.85 depending on dataset size and metric. (3) Fig. 17 (p. 15): some cells fall in the deceleration region, i.e. the warm start slows them, although the trend favours acceleration; the per-cell histograms (Figs. 21, 28) show the spread. (4) Sec. 5.2-5.3 (pp. 20-21), qualitative: final compliances of two example cells are described as comparable and the assembled Hook geometry as globally similar, with density differences inside cells (Figs. 29-31).

baseline.classical_method: The 'standard' two-level (macro + cell) SIMP-based TO of Merli et al. 2025 (ref. [15], Comput.-Aided Des. 179), using a homogeneous/uniform initial density guess (set by the cell's volume fraction) at the cell-level SIMP stage; this is the sole comparator, and it is run with the identical FE/SIMP machinery as the proposed method, differing only in the initial guess
baseline.implementation: The authors' own two-level SIMP code following ref. [15]: OC update of filtered compliance sensitivities, filter radius 1.5 element sizes, p = 1 at the coarse level and p = 3 at the cell level, implementation details referred to the 99-line code [32] (Sec. 2.1-2.2, pp. 3-4); language and libraries not stated
baseline.solver: Not stated (no mention of direct vs. iterative/multigrid FE solver for the elasticity problem); Sec. 3.4.2 (p. 12) mentions factorisation strategies for the energy-metric FE analyses [a direct solver is inferred, not stated]
baseline.hardware_ml: Not stated (same code/hardware as the classical arm; only the initial density field differs, so no separate ML hardware is used)
baseline.problem_size: Cell domain: uniform Cartesian mesh with N_e = 32 (32x32 elements per cell); parameter space dimension D = 17 (16 boundary-traction coefficients + 1 volume fraction) in 2D. Macro (training) problems A, B, C contribute 374, 290 and 320 raw optimised cells respectively (Table 1); held-out 2D test problem ('Hook', Problem D) has 486 cells. Dataset sizes after enrichment: 748-1,968 cells (context-based only) or 5,984-15,744 cells (context-based + 8x rotation/flip augmentation), Table 2
baseline.classical_iterations: Convergence-based stopping ('until convergence condition is reached') for both the classical and proposed arms; no numeric convergence threshold is given in this article
baseline.classical_time: Not stated -- no wall-clock times are reported anywhere; the only reported speed proxy is the iteration-count ratio beta (Table 5)
baseline.ml_time: Not stated (same iteration-count proxy as above)
baseline.training_time: Not applicable / none: the instance-based model performs a nearest-neighbour lookup with 'no training phase' (Sec. 3.3)
baseline.data_generation_cost: Not quantified in time or iterations. The archive holds the optimised cells of macro problems A-C (984 cells, Table 1) plus an equal number of context-based samples, each obtained by solving a cell TO with FEM-SIMP (Sec. 3.2.1, 3.2.3: m = n; Table 2: 1,968 cells at Index 3 [derived: 984 dedicated extra cell TO runs]); the 8x augmentation adds samples at no computational cost (Sec. 3.2.2). The conclusions note that each context-based sample needs a cell TO solve (p. 22). No break-even is computed
baseline.quality_metric: Compliance (SIMP objective, Eq. 1), computed by the same FE solve used to run the optimisation itself (not a surrogate prediction), for both the classical and proposed arms
baseline.quality_gap: Not quantified numerically. Sec. 5.2 (p. 20): for two example cells the final compliances are described as comparable, with slight differences in density distribution (Figs. 29-30, compliance histories plotted). Sec. 5.3 / Fig. 31 (pp. 20, 23): the assembled Hook geometry is globally similar, with variations mainly in the centre of individual cells. No per-cell or assembled compliance is tabulated

R1.evidence: Sec. 3.3-5.3 and Table 5: both arms run the same SIMP code to the same convergence check, so the iteration ratio is taken at convergence for both, and no fail marker holds. Matching is loose: the convergence criterion is never stated numerically (Sec. 2.2, p. 4), the warm start leads to different local optima (Sec. 5.2, p. 20), and the final-compliance match is shown only for two example cells (Figs. 29-30) and qualitatively for the assembled structure (Fig. 31), with no per-cell compliance for the 486 test cells. This is the §5.3 R1 partial case.

R2.evidence: The classical ('standard') and proposed arms use the identical FE/SIMP implementation and (implicitly) identical hardware; only the cell's initial density field differs (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 10). No re-test data, no abstract-vs-results baseline mismatch, no GPU-vs-CPU asymmetry, and no fixed-iteration-cap vs. convergence-based mismatch is present (both use the same convergence-based stopping), so none of R2(a)-(e) is evidenced; per the template convention, unsure/no adverse evidence defaults to pass.

R3.evidence: The instance-based model has no training phase (Sec. 3.3, p. 10), so there is no training cost. The data cost is reported only as sample counts: 984 cells from macro problems A-C plus an equal number of context-based samples, each needing its own cell TO solve (Tables 1-2, pp. 7-9; Sec. 3.2.1; p. 22), i.e. 984 dedicated extra cell optimisations at Index 3 [derived]. No time or iteration count is given for building the archive, and no amortization or break-even against the per-cell saving is computed. Costs reported without amortization are the §5.3 R3 partial case; the article does address the data cost, so the fail marker (no training or data cost at all) does not hold.

R4.evidence: Every returned cell design in both arms comes from the real FE/SIMP solve (not a surrogate prediction), and the volume fraction is a constraint of that solve [inferred: OC enforces it]. But compliance is reported only for two example cells (Figs. 29-30) and qualitatively for the assembled structure (Fig. 31), no infeasibility or failure count is given, and inter-cell continuity is argued qualitatively (Sec. 5.3, p. 20). The decelerated cells are visible only in the per-cell plots (Figs. 17, 21, 28).

reporting.n_test_cases: 1 held-out macro test problem (2D 'Hook', 486 cells), evaluated across 3 training-dataset sizes (Index 1-3), 2 enrichment strategies (context-based; context-based + augmentation) and 2 similarity-metric families (vector-based L1/L2; energy-based) -- one structure, many cells and configurations

notes: Included as a speed-stratum ML-for-TO article: an instance-based (nearest-neighbour / case-based) model retrieves a previously-optimised cell to warm-start the cell-level SIMP optimiser, replacing the homogeneous initial guess of the pre-existing two-level TO method of Merli et al. 2025 (ref. [15]), which is this article's sole and explicit baseline. method_family is coded 'other' because the technique is instance-based/case-based retrieval (explicitly contrasted in the text with surrogate models such as neural networks that learn a parametric mapping; Sec. 3.3) and is not covered by the schema's cnn/gan/vae/diffusion_flow/transformer/gnn/llm_agent/rl/neural_reparam/surrogate_mlp_gp categories. Scope judgment for the verifier: the article presents the retrieval as a machine-learning technique (keywords; Sec. 1 and 3.1), and nearest-neighbour retrieval is a standard instance-based learning method, but it is not on the §3.1 example list; if a verifier does not count it as a learned model, FT-NOML applies. ood_test = yes because the test macro-problem (Hook) is a structurally distinct problem never included in the archive (Table 1). seeds_or_variance = yes on the strength of the standard deviations of the nearest-neighbour distances (Tables 3-4) and the per-cell acceleration-ratio histograms (Figs. 21, 28); Table 5's means carry no explicit spread. No wall-clock timing is reported anywhere in the article; the entire speed claim rests on an iteration-count ratio (beta), which is used here as the speed proxy of PROTOCOL §3, criterion 2 ('fewer FE evaluations'). retest_candidate is false: no code-availability statement is given (only data on request, Data availability section, p. 23). Duplicate check: audit/pool/pool.csv searched by title on 2026-09-24; no second pool record found (this is the only pid for this article; it has no arXiv id). Related records by the same group, different studies [inferred from titles and abstracts]: P00367 (arXiv 2307.15665, two-level continuous TO) and P00729 (SSRN, neural-network multi-level TO). Incidental cross-reference, not a duplicate: this article's reference [16] is Y. Zhang et al., arXiv:1901.07761, the same article as pid P00176. No author named Jun Wang. Screening code was I-SPEED. Adjudication (2026-09-24): the first coder met the ScienceDirect captcha and coded abstract-only; the adjudicator read the RiuNet copy in full and based the record on the second coding, with R3 changed from fail to partial (the article reports the archive's size and says each context-based sample needs a cell TO, and it has no training phase) and several fields corrected: the second coding's R3 evidence attributed a phrase about the archive cost coming for free to Sec. 1, which the text does not contain (its no-cost statements concern data augmentation, pp. 1, 2, 8, and the mapping of context-based samples back to the parameter space, p. 7, not the cell TO solves); the implementation field now records the OC update and filter of Sec. 2.1; long verbatim quotations were replaced by paraphrases (PROTOCOL §7.4).

stratum.reason: The abstract (p. 1) and conclusions (Sec. 6, pp. 21-23) claim reduced computation time only qualitatively, so §5.1 rule 2 goes to the main text, whose quantitative comparison with the standard SIMP is the iteration-count acceleration ratio (Eqs. 6-7, p. 13; Table 5, p. 17). Fewer SIMP iterations are a cost proxy, so the stratum is speed.

claimed_speedup.reason: Table 5 (p. 17) gives 2.67 for the energy-based metric with Dataset Index 3 and augmentation, the configuration the conclusions recommend (p. 22); the highest cell, 2.86 (L2), is within 10 %. It is an averaged iteration ratio, not a time.

R1.reason: Both arms converge with the same SIMP code, so no fail marker holds, but the convergence criterion is not stated numerically (Sec. 2.2, p. 4) and final compliance is compared only for two example cells and qualitatively for the assembled structure (Figs. 29-31, pp. 20-23): the §5.3 R1 partial case.

R2.reason: Both arms use the same FE/SIMP code and differ only in the initial guess (Sec. 3.3, Fig. 10, pp. 9-11), and the claim is an iteration ratio, so solver and hardware cancel; the abstract has no baseline number and no marker (a)-(e) is established; unsure means pass.

R3.reason: There is no training phase (Sec. 3.3, p. 10), and the data cost is reported as sample counts, with each of the 984 context-based samples needing its own cell TO (Tables 1-2, pp. 7-9; p. 22), but never in time or iterations and without break-even. That is 'costs reported with no amortization' (§5.3 R3 partial), not a speed claim with no data cost at all; the second coder's supporting quotation does not occur in the text.

R4.reason: Returned cells are real SIMP outputs, but their compliance is shown only for two example cells (Figs. 29-30) and qualitatively for the assembly (Fig. 31), and no infeasibility or failure count is given (Sec. 5.2-5.3, p. 20): the §5.3 R4 partial case.
